Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Palex is trying to keep our audit intake minimal — the external team only needs a concise packet that proves two things: 1) all customer data for our tenant in the EU stays in EU-hosted private deploys (VPC peering/privatelink evidence) and 2) confirmation of SOC 2 boundary for hosted control plane telemetry (we need to understand whether any logs/metrics are forwarded outside EU).

Could you provide a small evidence bundle (one PDF + one spreadsheet is ideal) and a 1-paragraph statement we can include in our compliance package? Also, if there's a DocuSign acknowledgement for the VPC topology, that would close the loop.

Thanks,
Emma Holmes
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Palex Health

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Compact evidence set request: EU private hosting + SOC2 scope

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear ask.

Short answer: we can produce a compact evidence packet that contains: a one-page statement of residency and private peering architecture, the runbook excerpt showing VPC peering/privatelink endpoints for the EU deployment, a SOC 2 scope matrix (single-sheet) that highlights the control plane telemetry boundaries, and a condensed CAIQ answers PDF with the few questions auditors usually pull.

Attachments I will send (below) — I've looped in Irene to confirm the SOC 2 telemetry language and Marissa to trigger the DocuSign VPC acknowledgement. Can you confirm the contact to sign the DocuSign (Danielle or someone else)?

Deliverables planned: 1) redwood_eu_private_deploy_runbook_v1.pdf (diagram + peering table), 2) soc2_scope_matrix_eu_candidates.xlsx (highlighted rows), 3) caiq-responses-condensed.pdf (4 pages), 4) DocuSign link to acknowledgement.

Irene/Marissa — quick ask: please check the attached runbook for any operational caveats (e.g., temporary non-EU proxy during failover) and mark them clearly if they must be disclosed. We prefer to avoid language that implies cross-border telemetry for customer request traces.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Security Engagement Manager
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-02T09:16:00Z

Subject: Re: Compact evidence set request: EU private hosting + SOC2 scope

On 2026-12-01 12:04, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai wrote:
> Irene/Marissa — quick ask: please check the attached runbook for any operational caveats (e.g., temporary non-EU proxy during failover) and mark them clearly if they must be disclosed.

Thanks Sofia. I reviewed the runbook excerpt and SOC 2 matrix. Notes: 
- Residency statement: Accurate as drafted for customer-dedicated EU private deploys — all production inference traffic, model artifacts, and customer KV caches remain in EU regions (we reference eu-west-1 / europe-west2 depending on the tenant).
- Telemetry/Control plane: The control plane signals (orchestration heartbeats, instance health) are aggregated in a customer-scoped control plane in the EU by default. However, some anonymized, platform-level metrics (agg token throughput, instance-level telemetry that contains no customer content) are replicated to our global telemetry store which is currently hosted in the US for analytics (these are aggregated, non-customer-identifiable metrics).
- Failover caveat: In the extremely unlikely scenario of region-wide outage where the customer has authorized cross-border DR, there is a documented fallback path that routes to a warmed standby in a neighbouring region. We can omit DR-level fallback disclosure if the customer requires strict EU-only language, but we must then annotate that DR is out of scope for the statement.

Suggested language (one paragraph) for the packet: "Redwood Inference confirms that for Palex Health's EU private deployment, all inference requests, customer data, model artifacts, and KV caches are stored and processed in EU-designated infrastructure. Platform-level telemetry is collected for operational health within the EU; aggregated non-customer-identifiable metrics may be processed in Redwood's global analytics environment. Disaster recovery that would route customer workloads outside EU is not enabled by default and would require a contractual DR opt-in."

I'll send a redline for the SOC 2 matrix and flag the single row where the telemetry replication note must be explicit.

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
